episodes.194626: Scattered thunderstorms offshore of St George Island produced at least one waterspout that was photographed.
episodes.194861: An area of low pressure centered offshore of southern Oregon sent mid-level moisture northward and created an unstable air mass, leading to the development of a severe thunderstorm with strong straight line, downdraft winds in the city of Lakeview in Lake County, Oregon.
episodes.195790: Showers produced three waterspouts over southern Lake Michigan during the morning of September 7th.  One of the waterspouts came onshore as a brief landspout tornado northeast of Beverly Shores in northwest Indiana.
episodes.195792: A waterspout came onshore as a brief landspout tornado northeast of Beverly Shores during the morning of September 7th.  No damage was reported.
episodes.196430: Showers and thunderstorms tracked into western New York  as a shortwave trough and cold front crossed the area. A few of the thunderstorms became strong to severe. One storm developed a tornado in Allegany County. Heavy rainfall associated with the showers and storms did cause some Flash Flooding in Cattaraugus County.
episodes.196463: Conditions over the Eastern Great Lakes became favorable for waterspout development on September 7th as cool air aloft moved into the area within a large scale trough over the region. Showers that developed/moved over Lake Erie did produce a waterspout off of the lakeshore near Dunkirk on the afternoon of Saturday September 7th.
episodes.196548: A weak push of monsoon moisture and hot temperatures combined to fuel scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. A few storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.196558: A deep upper level trough approached from the west along with the associated surface low and fronts. A thin line of showers and thunderstorms developed along a cold front as it moved into the area. A portion of the line became severe and produce damaging wind gusts over the waters.
episodes.196628: A cold front produced gusty winds as it moved across the Chesapeake Bay on September 7.
episodes.196636: A deep upper level trough approached from the west along with the associated surface low and fronts. A thin line of showers and thunderstorms developed along a cold front as it moved into the area. A portion of the line became severe and produce damaging wind gusts over northeast NJ.
episodes.196661: Unsettled weather conditions prevailed across Puerto Rico through the first week of September as a retrograding upper level trough lingered in the region. The instability of the trough, diurnal heating, and low level moisture combined to generate widespread showers and thunderstorms across the region. Each day, accumulations ranged from 2 to 3 inches, with maximum amounts up to 5 inches in some areas. This led to several reports of mudslides, lightning, and gusty winds.
episodes.196698: A large cluster of thunderstorms developed near the center of an area of low pressure as it tracked just off the southeast South Carolina coast. The thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts across the Atlantic coastal waters.
episodes.196738: Wind gusts from isolated thunderstorms resulted in several downed trees near Blue River in Lane County. One of the trees fell onto a power line which disrupted local power.
episodes.196782: Monsoon moisture over northern Ariozna, very weak steering flow, and westerly winds provided ventilation aloft leading to slow-moving thunderstorms with locally heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.196982: After multiple days of off and on rain from the stalled boundary along the LA coast, more rain in association with that boundary fell across southeast Louisiana. This time, the heaviest rain fell closer to the coast in portions of Terrebonne and St. Charles parish where instances of flash flooding occured.
episodes.201066: At the surface, a trough lingered over Lake Erie, northern OH, and northwest PA during the morning of the 7th as a low moved north-northeastward, along a surface front, from northeastern Lake Ontario to southwestern QC. Behind the low, a northwesterly mean low-level flow of sufficiently-cold and moist air across relatively-warm Lake Erie yielded appreciable lake-induced instability and allowed several bands of lake-effect rain showers to stream southeastward over and downwind of the lake. Non-mesocyclonic waterspouts accompanied some of these showers offshore Conneaut, OH and Lake City, PA.

events.narrative: A severe thunderstorm along North 4th St, Highway 140, in Lakeview, Oregon generated strong downdraft straight line winds.  Power lines were tipped over and tree limbs were down, resulting in 710 customers that lost power.  The roof blew off the Pacific Power office building, into the road.
